title: Monet and Renoir masterpiece paintings reunited for rare London display
summary: Ahead of the Gallery’s major autumn exhibition, Renoir and Love (3 October 2026 – 31 January 2027), visitors are invited to an exciting sneak preview through the reunion of two of Impressionism's most celebrated paintings. For a limited period, Claude Monet's and Pierre-Auguste Renoir's La Grenouillère (1869) will be displayed together at the Gallery for the first time in nineteen years. Painted side by side from almost exactly the same viewpoint, the works capture a defining moment in the birth of Impressionism, offering a first glimpse into the artistic friendships, emotional storytelling and spirit of experimentation that will be explored throughout Renoir and Love. The display will remain on view until mid-September, before Renoir's painting is incorporated into the exhibition installation. The reunion of the two paintings has been made possible thanks to the generous loan of Renoir's painting from Nationalmuseum, Stockholm. During the summer of 1869, Monet and Renoir

title: Christie's to auction Monet landscape estimated at $12M-$16M in Paris
summary: As international celebrations mark the centenary of Claude Monet's death, Christie's announced the auction of Bord des falaises à Pourville by Claude Monet, estimated at €11–15 million. Encouraged by his dealer Paul Durand-Ruel, Monet travelled to Pourville in 1882 for what would become one of the most prolific periods of his career. Part of a landmark series within the artist's oeuvre, Bord des falaises à Pourville is further distinguished by its exceptional provenance, having come directly from Paul Durand-Ruel's personal collection. The painting will undoubtedly be the highlight of Christie's forthcoming sale of the Durand-Ruel Collection in Paris. A unique opportunity to celebrate the special esteem in which the master of Giverny held the dealer who remains one of the most influential figures in the history of art dealing. “There is only one person to whom I owe anything, and that is Durand-Ruel.” -- Claude Monet said to René

title: Zentrum Paul Klee to present first Swiss solo show for Florence Henri in 40 years
summary: She was a musician in Paris and London, she painted in Paris, Munich, Rome and Spain, attended courses by Paul Klee, among others, at the Bauhaus, and became, with her photographs, one of the most important representatives of ‘New Vision’. Florence Henri (1893–1982) moved at the centres of the European avant-garde and helped shape them to a considerable degree, particularly in the field of photography. From 29 August 2026 to 10 January 2027, in the context of the permanent exhibition Kosmos Klee, the Zentrum Paul Klee is showing the artist’s first solo exhibition in Switzerland for over 40 years. Florence Henri’s artistic beginnings coincide with a time of great political and social upheavals: before, during and after the world wars, artists all over Europe were seeking new forms of expression to represent appropriately or to deliberately deny social realities. title: Detroit Institute of Arts announces gift of 2,000+ Modern/Contemporary art from Silverman Family Estate
summary: The Detroit Institute of Arts (DIA) announced today it has received a transformative gift of more than 2,000 works of modern and contemporary art by nearly 500 artists, all generously donated from the Estate of Gilbert B. and Lila Silverman. The Silvermans were visionary collectors whose deep commitment to the DIA and the City of Detroit has shaped the museum’s relationship with contemporary art. This monumental gift adds substantially to the DIA’s renowned collection of modern and contemporary art. Broad in media, geography, and chronology, this significant gift includes artists books, decorative arts, drawings, furniture, jewelry, paintings, performance and documentation, periodicals, photographs, prints, sculpture, textiles, and time-based media. This gift enriches the holdings of several DIA departments: African American Art, American Art, European Sculpture and Decorative

title: Met Museum to showcase Louis C. Tiffany design drawings in new fall exhibition
summary: This fall, The Metropolitan Museum of Art will present Designing the Gilded Age: Drawings from the Studios of Louis C. Tiffany, a major exhibition exploring the creative process behind some of Tiffany Studios' most celebrated works. On view from October 22, 2026, through February 7, 2027, the exhibition brings together nearly 120 works from the Museum's collection—along with a select group of key loans—to examine the artistic range of Louis Comfort Tiffany and the collaborative studio that produced significant works of American decorative art. title: Pace Berlin presents 'Exquisite Corpse,' tracing Kiki Kogelnik's influence across generations
summary: Pace will present Exquisite Corpse, an exhibition curated by Loie Hollowell (b. 1983 Woodland, California, USA) in response to her appreciation of the influential Austro-American artist Kiki Kogelnik (b. 1935 Graz, Austria – d. 1997 Vienna, Austria). In conversation with two of Hollowell’s contemporaries, Sascha Braunig (b. 1983 Qualicum Beach, Canada) and Veronika Pausova (b. 1987, Prague, Czech Republic), Hollowell discovered that Kogelnik’s work had equally impacted their own practices. This exhibition will bring together works by all four cross-continental, multigenerational artists. “Exquisite corpse” is a collaborative parlor game invented by Surrealist artists in 1925. Players take turns either writing words or drawing sections of a body on a folded sheet of paper, hiding their contributions so the next person can see and respond to only the very end of the previous work. title: The Grolier Club will present photographs by Henry Wessel
summary: The Grolier Club presents a spotlight exhibition on photographs and books by Henry Wessel (1942–2018), curated by Grolier Club member Jack Gray from his collection. On view from September 8 through November 14, 2026, in the Club’s Second Floor Gallery, Henry Wessel – Photographs and Books features more than 65 photographs, including Wessel’s “Incidents” and “Traffic” portfolios in their entirety, and highlights from Wessel’s full body of work from more than four decades. A catalogue, published by The Grolier Club, will be available this autumn. Wessel first came to prominence in 1972 with a solo exhibition at The Museum of Modern Art, New York, and his practice initially centered on exhibitions with related catalogues. He later moved emphatically to making sequences of photographs intended as one work. These were issued as portfolios and published as books with minimal context. Curator Jack

title: RM Sotheby's to offer the first-ever Czinger 21C to appear at public auction
summary: RM Sotheby's will present the first-ever Czinger 21C to be offered at public auction during The Monterey Auction. Estimated at $2,300,000–$2,500,000 USD, the 2025 example marks a significant milestone for one of the most technologically advanced hypercars of the modern era and offers collectors the opportunity to acquire one of just 80 examples produced worldwide. Powered by an in-house developed twin-turbocharged 2.88-liter V-8 hybrid powertrain producing a combined 1,250 horsepower, the 21C HDF delivers extraordinary performance while remaining fully road legal in all 50 US states. The model has also established itself as a benchmark for modern performance, setting production-car lap records at five of California's premier circuits during Czinger's "California Gold Rush" program. title: Emily Kam Kngwarray exhibition to tour across Australia
summary: Generously supported by First Nations Arts Partner Wesfarmers Arts, the National Gallery Touring Exhibition will take Emily Kam Kngwarray’s (c.1910–1996) works from the national collection to five galleries across the country – offering Australians an unprecedented opportunity to experience the power, innovation and enduring legacy of her art. Beginning at Araluen Arts Centre in Mparntwe/Alice Springs on 9 April 2027, the exhibition will return Anmatyerr artist Kngwarray's work to the Central Desert, close to her home Country in Urapuntja/Utopia, before touring nationally. The exhibition will then travel to Cairns Art Gallery, Qld; Art Gallery of Western Australia, WA; Newcastle Art Gallery, NSW and Burnie Arts Centre, Tas. title: Judy Chicago exhibition in the Netherlands explores feminism and Jewish identity
summary: Revelations is a solo exhibition by iconic feminist artist Judy Chicago. Known for challenging the male-dominated art world, Chicago explores themes of gender, power, and social justice. Her focus on language, creation, and forgotten stories reflect her Jewish heritage. It is Chicago’s first solo presentation in the Netherlands. Judy Chicago (1939) gained prominence in the late 1960s for making work from a woman-centred perspective that challenged the male-dominated art world. Chicago’s work is characterised by a commitment to craft and experimentation, evident in her subject matter, methodology and choice of materials. Throughout her six-decade career, Chicago has addressed the absence of women in the Western cultural canon. She developed a distinctive visual language that gives visibility to women’s experiences. Her work engages with themes such as birth, masculinity, Jewish identity, power, extinction, and climate justice. The exhibition is named after an unpublished

title: Mari Nagem explores climate change and space exploration in new solo show
summary: CUE Art presents The Tropics, The Moon, and Mars, a solo exhibition by Brooklyn-based Brazilian artist Mari Nagem. The exhibition is on view at CUE’s gallery space at 137 W. 25th Street until September 26, 2026. Attendance during gallery hours (Wed–Sat, 12–6 pm) is free; no reservations are required. The Tropics, The Moon, and Mars is an immersive installation that unites light, sound, sculpture, painting, and digital experiments. Nagem constructs a post-natural tropical environment in which heat reorganizes relationships between bodies, technologies, geological formations, and living systems. The tropics appear as climate, home, and projection: a lived geography shaped by extraction, ecological transformation, and a long history of being imagined from elsewhere. title: William King Museum of Art announces new Jocelyn Mathewes exhibition
summary: William King Museum of Art (WKMA) in Abingdon, Virginia announced the opening of Jocelyn Mathewes: Para(site)dise. This new exhibition will be on view from August 20th, 2026 through January 10th, 2027 in WKMA’s United Company Contemporary Regional Gallery. Jocelyn Mathewes’ work, ranging from photography, to assemblage, to paper sculpture and video, centers on the theme of illness and corporeality: how do we deal with illness, especially chronic illness, in our day to day lives? In what ways are we allowed to be sick and in what ways are we expected to be strong? Above all, how do we navigate illness in a world which is not made to accommodate disabilities or, indeed, times of weakness? In our region, as in the rest of Appalachia, those who deal with pollution, addiction or disabilities face this struggle every day. title: Dayton Art Institute launches new website
summary: The Dayton Art Institute announced the launch of its newly redesigned website, made possible through support from the Bloomberg Philanthropies Digital Accelerator Program for Arts and Culture. The new website creates a more engaging, accessible and user-friendly online experience, making it easier for visitors, members, donors and the community to discover exhibitions, explore collections, purchase tickets, register for programs and connect with the museum in a digital space. Recognizing that digital innovation is essential for cultural organizations to better serve their communities, the Bloomberg Philanthropies Digital Accelerator Program provides funding and strategic support to help nonprofit arts organizations strengthen their technology infrastructure, develop sustainable digital practices and create more meaningful connections with audiences. title: CARA to host Johanna Hedva's first New York institutional exhibition
summary: CARA’s fall 2026 exhibition, Gravity, My / Favorite Enemy is Johanna Hedva’s first institutional exhibition in New York. Devoted to deviant forms of knowledge, Hedva’s practice moves between sculpture, installation, video, writing, and sound. Gravity, My / Favorite Enemy is the most ambitious presentation of their visual work, including pieces commissioned by CARA. The exhibition gathers time-based installation and video alongside newly produced sculptural wall paintings and a large-scale kinetic sculpture. “I like working with gravity, deterioration, materiality that’s destroyed over time, ruins; I try to make the abyss feel visceral and intimate and close for my viewer,” writes Hedva. title: Forum Gallery exhibition explores human connection across generations
summary: Continuing at Forum Gallery is Summer of Love, an exhibition presenting more than twenty modern and contemporary paintings, works on paper, quilts, and sculpture by seventeen artists. Physical connections flourish in works by Max Weber (1881-1961), Raphael Soyer (1899-1987), Chaim Gross (1902-1991) and Clio Newton (b. 1989). Following his immersion in the Parisian avant-garde between 1905 and 1909, Max Weber returned to the United States brimming with ideas that launched a pivotal early period of creative experimentation, ultimately spawning his own original, hybrid Cubism. Max Weber is widely regarded as the first American Cubist. At the height of this period in 1917, Weber painted The Sisters. title: Galerie Diurne to present Marcel Zelmanovitch's "Ratures & Artefacts" in Paris
summary: Galerie Diurne will open Ratures & Artefacts, a new exhibition by painter and textile artist Marcel Zelmanovitch, on September 17, 2026, bringing together five large-scale “rug-paintings” that turn irregularities, interruptions and visual accidents into the central language of the work. The exhibition will remain on view through November 13 at the gallery’s 45 rue Jacob space in Saint-Germain-des-Prés. For more than four decades, Zelmanovitch has worked at the intersection of painting and textile, exploring what happens when gesture, color, texture and light leave the canvas and enter the physical world of woven material. His practice eventually led him to develop what he calls “rug-paintings”: signed works conceived with the expressive ambitions of painting but realized through hand-knotting and textile craftsmanship. title: Historic agreement sees RCA & Norwich University of the Arts launch jointly awarded undergraduate degrees
summary: The Royal College of Art and Norwich University of the Arts have entered into a historic agreement to establishjointly awarded undergraduate degrees, creating a new model of creative higher education collaboration in the UK. The aim is to strengthen academic quality and support regional growth which will open new routes to postgraduate study and reinforce the UK's global leadership in creative education. The partnership represents the only current opportunity to study undergraduate degrees awarded by the Royal College of Art, the world’s leading art and design university and a specialist postgraduate institution. title: London Museum launches search for new DJ Collective
summary: London Museum has today announced its search for a new DJ collective to perform regularly in its new free permanent galleries, opening in Smithfield on 28 November 2026. In collaboration with iconic London chicken shop Morley’s and Hive Curates, the Sound of London DJ Collective will shift the museum’s mood from day to night, curating the soundtrack for the weekly late opening hours - every Friday and Saturday night until 11PM. Applications are open until 14 August 2026 HERE. The museum will bring together 12 emerging DJs from across London’s boroughs - encompassing a range of genres, backgrounds and ages and selected with the support of special guest judges, representing voices from across London’s music scene. Through regular paid performances, DJs will have the chance to bring their own perspectives and creative energy

title: Frenzi Rigling receives Lower Austria's 2026 Recognition Award for Visual Arts
summary: Artist Frenzi Rigling has been named the recipient of the 2026 Lower Austria Recognition Award in the Visual Arts category, honoring a practice that has evolved over decades through painting, drawing, textiles and installation. Born in Schaffhausen, Switzerland, in 1958, Rigling now lives and works between Obermarkersdorf in Lower Austria and Vienna. Her work often begins with the ordinary: objects, materials and visual details drawn from her immediate surroundings. From these modest starting points, she creates layered installations and artworks that reflect on the rhythms of everyday life, the passage of time and the fragility of human existence. title: Group exhibition examines contemporary African cities across multiple Dakar venues
summary: Presented as part of the OFF Programme of the 2026 Dakar Biennale and Partcours, Palimpsest of African Cities is the latest edition of the DIG WHERE YOU STAND programme initiated by the African Artists' Foundation and taking place in several venues in Dakar, Senegal, from the 20th of November 2026 to the 28th of February 2027. This group exhibition brings together artists, architects, photographers, filmmakers, and researchers to explore the forces, narratives, and everyday dynamics that shape contemporary African cities. Conceived in partnership with KADIST, the African Artists’ Foundation (AAF), and the Institut français du Sénégal, the exhibition approaches the city as a space in constant rewriting, where memories, everyday uses, architectures, mobilities, and imaginaries overlap and interact. title: Exhibition Illuminates the Legacy of Dr. Samella Lewis
summary: The Claremont Lewis Museum of Art exhibition Samella! Black as Lacquer and Iron illuminates the extraordinary life and profound influence of Dr. Samella Lewis as an art historian, educator, philanthropist, and artist. Curated by her Scripps student Francine Farr, the exhibition includes works by Claude Lewis, Harmon Outlaw, Alison Saar, Howard Smith and others, as well as drawings and prints by Samella Lewis. A seminal figure in 20th-century American art, Samella Sanders Lewis (1923-2022) was a trailblazing art history professor at Scripps College and considered the first American woman polymath of African descent to receive a PhD in the history of art. Her life and global legacy celebrate and perpetuate the visual arts not only of African Americans and Africans but also of Asians, Asian Americans, Austronesians, and other indigenous

title: Alan Bean's Apollo 12 Lunar Surface-Flown Hammer sells for $812,500
summary: Exceptional artifacts from the Apollo program, many flown to the Moon and carried by astronauts during humanity’s greatest era of exploration, propelled Heritage’s July 23-24 Space Exploration Signature® Auction to $3,114,908 as collectors from around the world competed for museum-quality relics tied directly to the history of lunar exploration. The result made the auction the largest at Heritage, the world’s leading Space Exploration auctioneer, since The Armstrong Family Collection III Space Exploration Signature Auction brought $4,636,912 in July 2019. The auction’s undisputed centerpiece was Alan Bean’s Apollo 12 Lunar Module Flown and Surface-Used Geological Hammer, which realized $812,500. title: Ivorian artist Nuits Balnéaires unveils autobiographical project 'Eboro'
summary: Over the past few years, Nuits Balnéaires has established a practice that is hybrid in many ways. The Ivorian artist moves between fine art, fashion, and research-based practices; his influences are a blend of cinema, literature, theater, performance, and cultural history; his life is both rooted in the small coastal town of Grand-Bassam, east of Abidjan, and involved with many more international cultural communities. Eboro was created as part of the Latitudes program of the Fondation d’entreprise Hermès, of which Nuits Balnéaires is the second laureate. This project introduces a more autobiographical dimension to Nuits Balnéaires’ work. The project begins in Dakar, Senegal, where, on July 22, 1986, his uncle, Noël X. title: University of Sunderland celebrates innovative NHS photography project
summary: The University of Sunderland has hosted colleagues and guests to celebrate an innovative photography project which has evolved into a new movement aiming to give NHS staff a voice through creativity. NHS Darkroom is a participatory photography research project led by Sunderland lecturer, photographer and former NHS nurse, Johannah Churchill, in partnership with Newcastle Hospitals Charity. Since 2022, NHS staff across clinical and non-clinical roles have taken part each year, learning darkroom processes and using them to print images of their own working lives. Rather than solely being photographed by Johannah, they collaborate - she works with participants to create their own images and print them by hand, shaping how their working lives are seen and understood.
